explanation: Arabic al-kuhl was kohl, a fine powder used to darken the eyelids. Alchemists applied the name to any fine powder or refined essence, and by the 1700s to the spirit in wine.

claims.text: 'Alcohol' comes from Arabic al-kuhl, 'the kohl', a fine powder used as eye make-up.
Al-kuhl did not mean date wine, a healing oil or a perfume.
European alchemists used 'alcohol' for any fine powder or refined essence.
By the 1700s 'alcohol' meant the intoxicating spirit in wine and other drinks.
